title: Windows CC build fails with MSVC C1060 compiler out of heap space
signature: compiler is out of heap space|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Conditional Compilation
failed_jobs.symptom: MSVC C1060 error: compiler is out of heap space in oneDNN and openvino_reference targets

key_errors: C:\BuildTools\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.42.34433\include\xmemory(1500,1): error C1060: compiler is out of heap space [openvino_reference.vcxproj]
memory_desc_wrapper.hpp(733,5): error C1060: compiler is out of heap space [dnnl_cpu_x64.vcxproj]
primitive_attr.hpp(108,1): error C1060: compiler is out of heap space [dnnl_cpu_x64.vcxproj]
root_cause: The Windows CI runner ran out of compiler heap memory (MSVC error C1060) while building multiple targets in parallel — openvino_reference.vcxproj and several oneDNN vcxproj targets all hit the heap limit simultaneously. This is a transient infrastructure-level constraint: too many parallel MSBuild compilations competing for process heap on the shared runner.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed jobs — the failure is transient and typically resolves on retry
Consider reducing the MSBuild /maxcpucount parallelism for the Conditional Compilation job to lower peak memory pressure
Consider adding /Zm flag to increase compiler heap size in the MSVC build options
prevention_strategies: Reduce parallel compilation processes in the Windows CC CI job or increase runner memory allocation. Setting /maxcpucount:4 or lower in the MSBuild invocation can help avoid simultaneous heap exhaustion.
historical_context: No prior occurrence of this exact pattern found in repo-memory.
